resolved_1788847609608_5ad1s.web_spread_summary: The 'Lenna' image is the most widely used standard test image in the history of digital image processing. Its ubiquity stems from its inclusion in the USC-SIPI database in the early 1970s. Despite its origin as a centerfold, it has been used for decades in academic research to demonstrate compression, edge detection, and restoration algorithms. Its use has also sparked significant scholarly discourse regarding gender representation in computer science.
